assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, insulinotropic activity of GLP-1(7-36)) led to a therapeutic class that has transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and shows cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity of mechanism and breadth of human impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Decisive basic contributions came from Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (biology, gut-hormone actions, translation to therapy) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide form and its insulinotropic activity). Knudsen's pharmaceutical development of long-acting analogues is also decisive for the drugs, and Habener-linked early work is not on the supplied credit list. The three-person limit forces a choice between discovery and drug development; I favour the discovery-side trio but this is genuinely contestable.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed repeatedly and independently, and clinical outcome trials are robust. Recognition is timely and arguably urgent given the scale of clinical use.
uncertainties: Fair allocation between discovery scientists and drug developers is unresolved.
Mojsov's priority relative to other early GLP-1 work is debated and I cannot verify the details independently.
Long-term safety and durability of benefit are still being characterised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically targeted optical control of excitable cells created a general experimental method that reshaped causal neuroscience and physiology, from circuits to behaviour and into early clinical translation. The microbial opsin discovery and its transfer to neurons are original and conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and demonstration of millisecond control in neurons (Deisseroth, Boyden) are both essential; Miesenboeck's earlier genetically targeted photostimulation adds a further claim. Six credited names cannot fit; I choose the channelrhodopsin discovery side plus the neuronal implementation, leaving Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck as notable omissions.
assessment.maturity: Very widely used for two decades with independent confirmation; clinical use is only emerging (retinal restoration), but as a tool the impact is mature. Timely.
uncertainties: Priority disputes among Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenboeck are not resolved by the supplied credit.
Bamberg's omission would be hard to justify within a three-person cap.
Whether tool-based recognition fits the prize relative to therapeutic discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, establishing a new therapeutic modality (living drugs) with strong conceptual and clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early CAR design with costimulation; June led the first durable clinical responses in CLL with 4-1BB CARs; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and gene-engineered T-cell trials. Eshhar, a foundational figure for CAR concept, is not among the credited names, which weakens the completeness of the configuration. The selected three are the best fit among those supplied.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and years of follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic cancers; solid tumours remain largely unresolved. Recognition is reasonably timely.
uncertainties: Absence of Eshhar from the credited names limits a fair configuration.
Rosenberg's contribution is adoptive cell therapy broadly rather than CARs specifically.
Toxicity, relapse and limited solid-tumour efficacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR is a central regulator of growth and nutrient sensing, with broad relevance to metabolism, ageing, cancer and immunology. The discovery chain from rapamycin to TOR genes to a conserved signalling network is original and has lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genes in yeast and established TOR as a growth controller; Schreiber's work on the rapamycin-FKBP12 complex defined the drug-target logic. Sabatini and others cloned mammalian mTOR and defined complexes; the supplied credit allows only three. Sabatini's inclusion is complicated by documented institutional controversy that I cannot fully assess here, and the mTOR identification also involved other groups not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed across organisms; therapeutic exploitation (rapalogs in transplant and oncology) is established, though broader disease claims are still maturing.
uncertainties: Competing credit for mammalian mTOR identification across several groups.
Sabatini's standing given reported professional controversies, which I cannot verify.
Rapamycin pharmacology itself had earlier contributors not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defines how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunology. This is a clean mechanistic discovery that opened a field.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAMP as the second messenger and cGAS as its synthase, the decisive step; Barber identified STING as the adaptor. Ishikawa independently contributed to STING identification, with Wu and Sun as Chen-lab co-authors. A two-person prize of Chen and Barber is the most defensible fit.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many independent labs; therapeutic translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has been slow so far, so clinical validation is not yet mature.
uncertainties: Ishikawa's claim to STING identification relative to Barber.
Clinical benefit of pathway modulation is unproven.
Recognition may be somewhat early relative to therapeutic maturation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defining Lgr5 stem cells and growing self-organising intestinal organoids from single adult stem cells created a durable platform for studying tissue biology, disease modelling and personalised medicine.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the conceptual and experimental program and Sato carried out the key organoid culture work; both are clearly decisive and the credited pair is compact. Other organoid pioneers (pluripotent-derived, e.g. Sasai) are outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Broad independent adoption with growing clinical-translation use; the scientific impact is established, though the clinical benefit of organoids remains largely prospective.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be framed around Lgr5 stem cells or organoid technology.
Overlap with other organoid lineages not captured by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new intracellular signalling pathway from the ER to the nucleus, with Ire1-Hac1/XBP1 splicing as an unusual mechanism and wide relevance to secretory physiology, metabolism, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori's convergent identification of the signalling mechanism is the clear core; the pair is a clean and fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is deeply confirmed and conserved; therapeutic translation is still developing but the basic discovery is mature and long recognised.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is limited so far.
Proximity to other protein-quality-control recognition may weigh on timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstration that TNF is a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis, validated by anti-TNF antibodies, transformed treatment of rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn's disease and psoriasis, and proved the broader concept of cytokine blockade.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini established the rationale and the first clinical proof; antibody engineering and TNF biology involved other contributors who are not in the credited list, but the pair is a coherent fit for a translational prize.
assessment.maturity: Decades of clinical use and independent confirmation; timing is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether a translational-medicine prize here is competitive against newer discoveries.
Contributions of antibody-engineering and TNF-biology scientists outside the credited pair.
